name: mtld_diversity_anchor_relative
mechanism: McCarthy & Jarvis 2010 MTLD (Modified Type-Token Ratio Dynamic): forward and backward factor counting when TTR falls to 0.72, averaged. Anchor-relative: measures diversity of changed/inserted tokens vs anchor baseline. Rewards maintaining or improving lexical diversity in creative rewrites despite the weak negative TTTR-creativity correlation (Wundt inverted-U: diversity must be contextually appropriate, not maximized blindly).
reasoning: Previous TTR attempts were too naive (raw type-token ratio inversely predicts creativity on 2-sentence texts). MTLD properly captures the dynamism of lexical diversity — a fresh approach measures whether creative elaborations maintain semantic coherence through sustained vocabulary variation. Anchor-relative focus isolates the rewrite's diversity contribution from baseline. Differs from all incumbents by implementing factor-counting correctly (forward+backward passes with partial-factor weighting at boundaries).

name: word_frequency_confound_residuals
mechanism: Residualization via scipy.linalg.lstsq: regress content-token surprisal on log-frequency to isolate novelty from rarity confound. Extract residuals = surprisal independent of word frequency. High positive residuals indicate conceptually surprising tokens despite common usage (novelty unconfounded). Calibrated via lstsq coefficient estimation on reference wordfreq lexicon.
reasoning: Incumbents conflate surprisal with lexical rarity (frequent words have predictable contexts; rare words are inherently surpriseful). This scorer directly de-confounds via regression residuals — the proper statistical technique. Differs from all prior attempts by: (1) explicit residualization (not just gating), (2) column-stacked design matrix for robust lstsq, (3) anchor-relative changed-token focus. Targets the causal-graph node 'word_frequency_confound' where surprisal is inflated by rarity without conceptual novelty.
reasoning_alt: Residualization separates signal from confound. By regressing surprisal on frequency and keeping residuals, we measure whether tokens are surprising *given their own frequency class* — true conceptual novelty. Addresses load-bearing path: surprisal/lexical_rarity confound in causal graph (edge from word_frequency_confound to surprisal, high confidence).

name: bigram_transition_improbability
mechanism: Bigram-level surprisal via independence-model divergence: for adjacent content-word pairs (w1, w2), compute surprisal = -log2(P(w1) * P(w2)). High surprisal indicates conceptually distant or novel word combinations (collocational surprise). Inverted-U calibration (Wundt curve peak at ~22 bits): rewards moderate surprise (creative combinations), penalizes extreme surprise (incoherent jumps). Gaussian response: Exp[-(surp - 22)^2 / (2 * 6^2)].
reasoning: Bigram-level surprisal captures distant semantic association (remote_association causal node footprint). Unlike token-level surprisal (confounded with rarity), bigram improbability isolates collocational novelty: common words in unexpected juxtaposition. No incumbent properly computes conditional probability or joint divergence; most use only unigram stats. Inverted-U response (Wundt curve from causal graph edges) penalizes extreme word combinations that violate coherence. This differs from all prior work by: (1) explicit bigram probability model, (2) Gaussian response curve (not linear), (3) focus on semantic distance through co-occurrence improbability.
